riskReasons: Accepted name, supported taxon, narrow deeply cut recurved lobes and red-purple seasonal sequence are consistent.
The separate identity of ‘Green Trompenburg’ is documented by an independent RHS accepted profile.
Published size frameworks differ substantially but the conflict is horticultural rather than an identity dispute.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with all RC-001–RC-010 records and all other approved Catalogue assignments. It is distinct from RC-001 ‘Bloodgood’ by its narrow, deeply divided lobes with recurved or rolled margins, and distinct from the accepted separate cultivar ‘Green Trompenburg’ by foliage colour, scale and profile. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The accepted working name follows RHS and Missouri Botanical Garden usage. ‘Green Trompenburg’ is a separate accepted cultivar, not a colour form or synonym. No other synonym is approved.

content.summary: An upright red-purple Japanese maple distinguished by narrow, deeply divided lobes whose margins roll or curve downward, with foliage becoming greener later in summer before turning orange-red to crimson in autumn.
content.habit: Upright deciduous shrub or small tree, developing a comparatively tall crown over time. Source frameworks range from a medium garden tree to a substantially larger mature specimen.
content.leafForm: Palmate leaves with seven, sometimes seven to nine, long narrow lobes divided deeply toward the base; the recurved or rolled margins create a characteristic convex appearance.

seasonal.spring: Foliage emerges deep red-purple to dark reddish purple.
seasonal.summer: Colour is retained well into the season but may shift toward reddish green or bronze by late summer.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn orange-red to showy crimson red.

size.qualifier: RHS gives 2.5–4 m high and wide at 10–20 years; Missouri Botanical Garden gives 15–25 ft high and 10–15 ft wide. Retain both as contextual published frameworks.

content.cultivation: Grow in moist, organically rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Provide shelter from strong winds and afternoon protection in hotter climates; avoid hot, dry sites and maintain soil moisture to limit scorch.
content.diagnostic: Compared with RC-001 ‘Bloodgood’, ‘Trompenburg’ has more narrowly divided lobes with conspicuously recurved or rolled edges. ‘Green Trompenburg’ is a separate green-leaved accepted cultivar and must not be merged. Leaf shape and colour support comparison but do not independently authenticate a clone.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, taxon, distinctive recurved narrow-lobed foliage and seasonal colour sequence; moderate confidence in mature size because RHS and Missouri Botanical Garden use materially different ranges.
content.unresolvedIssue: The broad mature-size divergence remains unresolved beyond preserving both source frameworks; the Missouri Botanical Garden origin account was not independently traced to a primary Arboretum Trompenburg record.
